clue.text: Conscious that a monarch should be held in high regard

indicators.note: something held in another is kept within it, so these two pieces sit inside the regard word

parts.note: awe is reverent high regard
R stands for Rex or Regina, a king or queen

explanation.surface: Someone is mindful that a king or queen must be treated with great respect.
explanation.definitionFit: To be aware of something is to be mindful or cognisant of it.

clue.text: Jack ordered retsina; this man wouldn't!

parts.note: a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, and AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: the letters of the Greek wine are put in a new order here

explanation.surface: A sailor asked for Greek wine, which a teetotaller would never do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like asking for a drink in a bar, but it rearranges RETSINA into STAINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller refrains from alcohol, so would never order a glass of wine.

clue.text: Poison-a coniferous fruit contains it

indicators.note: one piece containing another holds it inside, so the fruit word wraps around the next word

parts.note: the fruit of a conifer is its cone

explanation.surface: A pine cone is said to hold a toxic substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkshood, the plant source, yields a deadly toxin also known by this name.

clue.text: And Wilderness is Paradise "(Omar Khayyam)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: the missing last word of the famous Rubaiyat line in FitzGerald's translation

explanation.walkthrough: The line from FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam ends with an archaic word meaning 'enough'; the clue prints the line with its final word left out.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word for sufficient closes the quoted Rubaiyat verse.

clue.text: A man needs skill to get capital cover

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man
address in its older sense means dexterity or adroitness

explanation.surface: A man requires ability to win a top cover in a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' here means of the head (Latin caput), so a capital cover is something worn on the head; ADDRESS meaning skill is an older usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A hat or ornamental covering is worn on top, the capital part of a person.

clue.text: Replaced the cartoonist with little warning

indicators.note: letters replaced are put back in new places, a rearrangement signal here

explanation.surface: The newspaper's cartoonist was sacked and swapped out suddenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replaced' reads as a cartoonist being sacked, but it shuffles THE CARTOONIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done hurriedly comes with scarcely any advance notification.

clue.text: Food and drink for the assembly

explanation.surface: Food and drink are provided for a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is what one habitually eats; a Diet is also a legislative assembly, as in Japan's.

clue.text: A German enters cathedral city with enthusiasm

indicators.note: pieces that enter another go inside it, so these letters sit within the city

parts.note: Ely is a small English cathedral city in Cambridgeshire
German gives GER

explanation.surface: A German tourist arrives in a cathedral city full of excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something keenly means doing it with zeal.

clue.text: Protested when given glossy material

explanation.surface: Demonstrators made their point while dressed in shiny cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest by occupation, so to have staged one is to have protested; satin is a shiny silk fabric.

clue.text: Display notice cancelling the exhibition

explanation.surface: A sign goes up announcing the exhibition has been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt is to display oneself; a sign saying the show is off cancels it.

clue.text: Pureed fruit is sheer bliss-it's an illusion

parts.note: a fool is a British pudding of pureed fruit folded into cream
is contracts to 's
paradise is a state of perfect happiness

explanation.surface: A fruit dessert is heavenly, though its pleasures may be imaginary.
explanation.walkthrough: A FOOL is a British dessert of pureed fruit and cream; 'is' becomes the S of the possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of happiness based on false belief is a delusion.

clue.text: Cunning, slender-framed oriental

indicators.note: something framed has a border around it, so the slender word surrounds the next letter

parts.note: slight means slim or slender
E for East, the Orient

explanation.surface: A slim figure from the East is crafty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterous trickery, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: Not in favour of laying a snare

parts.note: a gin is a trap for catching animals

explanation.surface: Someone opposes setting traps for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect form of against, used to mean opposed to.

clue.text: Pass over in Panama

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
on can mean over or upon

explanation.surface: Someone crosses over while in Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition indicates a place found in Panama: Colon is the port city at the Caribbean end of the canal.
explanation.definitionFit: Colon is a Caribbean port city in that Central American country, at the canal's northern end.

clue.text: Show delight when King George is at home

parts.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone is happy when the King is in residence.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad smile shows pleasure.

clue.text: Quick drink around teatime

indicators.note: one piece placed around another encloses it, so the drink wraps the time

parts.note: ale is beer
four o'clock is a traditional teatime, and IV is Roman four

explanation.surface: A fast drink taken at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' is the old sense of living, as in the quick and the dead; teatime is four o'clock, giving Roman IV.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its old meaning is living, as in the phrase 'the quick and the dead'.

clue.text: A group of players held in reserve

parts.note: a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team is kept back as reserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put by is kept apart for later use.

clue.text: Have to condense one's speech, of course

parts.note: need means must or have to
to condense a speech is to have less to say

explanation.surface: Someone naturally must shorten their address.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase meaning obviously, it goes without saying.

clue.text: Grimaced and produced Identikit pictures?

explanation.surface: Someone pulled a face while building police likenesses.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull faces is to grimace; literally, an Identikit operator assembles likenesses of suspects.

clue.text: Feel inclined to be smart

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to show intelligence.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be strongly tempted; taken literally it means to possess a fine intellect.

clue.text: Difficult head with few finer feelings

parts.note: hard means difficult
nut is slang for head

explanation.surface: A troublesome leader lacks sensitivity.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough, unsentimental person is hard to deal with or move emotionally.

clue.text: It's a new concoction and should be agitated

indicators.note: a concoction mixes ingredients together, so these words are mixed up

explanation.surface: A newly mixed brew should be stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' turns IT'S A NEW into the phrase; the apostrophe is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a stew is an idiom for being anxious or flustered.

clue.text: Criticise the fish

explanation.surface: Someone finds fault with the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain pettily; a carp is a freshwater fish.

clue.text: Venomous creature needs firm, supportive underwear

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
a bra is underwear that gives support

explanation.surface: A poisonous snake needs a firm brassiere.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobra is a venomous hooded snake.

clue.text: Against a hat being quite acceptable

parts.note: V for versus, against
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Opposing a hat is perfectly reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something legitimate or sound is acceptable.

clue.text: Henry and Alfred get an equal share

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
Alf is short for Alfred

explanation.surface: Two men divide the takings evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: Splitting fifty-fifty gives each party one of two equal parts.

clue.text: Sore cheek

explanation.surface: A painful cheek.
explanation.definitionFit: A gall is a sore caused by chafing; gall also means impudence or nerve.

clue.text: The French in charge of non-clerics

parts.note: la is French for the

explanation.surface: French officials in command of laymen.
explanation.definitionFit: Laic means lay, relating to people who are not clergy.

clue.text: Belgian becomes resident in Asia

indicators.note: the Belgian word becomes another by rearranging its letters

explanation.surface: A Belgian moves to Asia and settles there.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bengali is a native of Bengal, in Bangladesh and eastern India.

clue.text: Mandela's ticked over partly by being flexible

indicators.note: only part of the words is taken, the run lying within them

explanation.surface: Mandela's clock ticked over, and he was adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elastic can stretch and bend, so is pliable.

clue.text: I'll burst a blood-vessel in the army

indicators.note: to burst into something is to break inside it, so the I'll word goes inside the vessel

parts.note: an artery is a blood vessel
the apostrophe is dropped, giving the letters as written

explanation.surface: Someone fears a blood vessel will rupture from army life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burst a blood-vessel' reads as an idiom for a fit of rage, but 'burst' is the container signal here; artillery is one branch of an army, so 'in the' links it.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the branch of an army operating big guns.

clue.text: Many birds of prey require hoods

parts.note: C is Roman 100, many
owls are nocturnal raptors

explanation.surface: Lots of raptors need head coverings.
explanation.definitionFit: Cowls are hoods worn by monks.
